learningObjectives: Explain the purpose of an SLA and its goal and deadline milestones
Distinguish Case Urgency from Assignment Urgency and how Get Next Work uses them
Apply SLAs at the Case Type, Stage, Process, and Step levels (and know the Create Stage exception)
Configure goals, deadlines, and escalation actions in App Studio

elements.description: Establishes a work-completion deadline to enforce on-time performance. Can be defined on an ASSIGNMENT or the overall CASE, and uses MILESTONES (goal, then deadline) to mark expected turnaround times.

elements.text: Think of a delivery target and a late threshold. Reaching either milestone only performs what was configured: a priority change, a notification or another action. A deadline is not a universal instruction to close the request.

elements.description: Goal and deadline use the SLA’s configured start reference. Case-resolution configuration can refer to this Case, its parent or the top-level Case.
items: GOAL — desired completion time, normally the earlier target; calculate from the configured start reference
DEADLINE — the longest time work MAY take before it is 'late'

elements.description: When a milestone is missed, the SLA can increase Urgency AND run an escalation: NOTIFY (assignee, manager, participants, or Case creator), REASSIGN to another user/queue, or RESOLVE the Case. Repeating post-deadline escalation is covered by the passed deadline interval.

elements.description: For a calendar-time policy, Goal at day 3 can notify; Deadline at day 7 can reassign; a passed deadline interval of three days with one event can resolve still-open work at day 10. Configure every action explicitly and account for processing delay and calendars. The post-deadline Rule configuration is covered in SA-M16.
Urgency is numeric priority with maximum 100:
items: CASE Urgency — priority of the Case itself
ASSIGNMENT Urgency — initial value equals Case Urgency (default 10); Stage/Process-level SLA adjustments affect Case Urgency

elements.description: Set the Case Type’s initial urgency in Settings. Updating a Case’s urgency supplies the new value for new Assignments, not existing ones. This does not prevent an existing Assignment’s own SLA from adjusting its urgency.

Pega prioritizes work by Urgency. GET NEXT WORK hands users the highest-Urgency Assignment they can perform first, so high-priority work finishes on time. Design SLAs/Urgency so the right work outranks the rest.

elements.term: Where SLAs apply (and the Create Stage exception)
elements.description: SLAs apply to Case Types, Stages, Processes, and Collect-information/Approval Steps. EXCEPTION: the Create Stage cannot have a goal, deadline, or escalation — it collects data before Case processing begins.

Use the appropriate Case or lifecycle-element Goal & deadline configuration. Case resolution offers Custom SLA, Existing SLA or Never, and This/Parent/Top-level Case anchors. Do not assume every lifecycle panel exposes all Case-resolution options. The linked 24.2 challenge configures the Schedule repair Step; the supplemental topic now uses Pega Infinity Studio terminology.

Configure notification recipients and message at the relevant goal and deadline. The supplemental Case/Stage/Process instructions describe Creator and Participants. General SLA escalation also includes reassignment or resolution; available controls depend on the selected context.

elements.caption: SLAs apply at Case Type, Stage, Process, and Step (Collect-info/Approval) levels — but never on the Create Stage.

elements.title: SLA Configuration Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Goal vs. Deadline direction
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Goal is the desired target; deadline marks lateness. Neither inherently guarantees a warning, reassignment or resolution without configured actions.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure responses at each milestone and use the intended start reference.

examPitfalls.title: Create Stage has NO SLA
examPitfalls.trapDescription: You cannot set a goal/deadline or escalation action on the Create Stage — it collects data before Case processing starts.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Apply SLAs on Case Type, Stages (not Create), Processes, and Collect-info/Approval Steps.

examPitfalls.title: Case Urgency vs. Assignment Urgency
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Case Urgency = the Case's priority; Assignment Urgency = one task's priority. Initial Assignment Urgency = Case Urgency; default 10, max 100, increase value 1–100.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set initial Urgency on the Case Type Settings tab; Stage/Process SLA increases affect Case Urgency.

examPitfalls.title: Case update versus task SLA
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Changing Case urgency does not retroactively initialize existing Assignments. This is not a rule that an existing Assignment’s own SLA cannot change urgency.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Keep Case-value inheritance separate from task-level SLA adjustments.

examPitfalls.title: Get Next Work uses Urgency
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask how Pega determines which Assignment a user receives when clicking 'Get Next Work.' Candidates say FIFO (first in, first out). Get Next Work selects the Assignment with the highest Urgency value — not the oldest one.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Tune Urgency so the most important work outranks the rest across Case Types.

examPitfalls.title: Calculate time from / Use SLA options
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Case-resolution settings offer Custom/Existing/Never and This/Parent/Top-level Case start references. Do not attribute every option to every lifecycle panel.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Reuse an Existing SLA for consistency; pick the right start reference for nested Cases.

examPitfalls.title: SLA vs. passed deadline (escalation)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks what term describes the action taken after a Deadline is passed. Candidates say 'SLA breach action.' The specific Pega term is Escalation Action — it is configured on the SLA rule and triggers automatically after the Deadline interval elapses.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure post-deadline recurrence on the SLA Rule with the event limit and Assignment completion policy, not an invented list of arbitrary extra milestones.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA asks an SA to explain the difference between an SLA goal and an SLA deadline. Which answer is correct?

options.text: The goal is how long the work should take (earlier, desired target); the deadline is the longest it may take before it is 'late' (later, mandatory limit). Both are measured from when the work started.
The goal and deadline are synonymous and fire the same action at the same time.
The deadline fires first as a warning; the goal fires later as the hard limit.
The goal is set by the business; the deadline is a fixed Pega default that cannot change.

practiceQuiz.hint: Goal = should (earlier); Deadline = must/late (later); measured from start.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The goal is the desired turnaround; the deadline marks lateness, with the configured start reference. They are distinct milestones and need not use the same actions.

optionExplanations.A: The goal is the desired turnaround; the deadline marks lateness, with the configured start reference.
optionExplanations.B: They are distinct milestones and need not use the same actions.
optionExplanations.C: This reverses desired target and late threshold.
optionExplanations.D: The deadline is configurable, not an immutable platform default.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An incomplete Case starts at urgency 10. Its SLA has a four-hour goal with +10 urgency and a 24-hour deadline with +10 urgency, and no resolution action. Assuming timely event processing, what urgency values follow the milestones?

options.text: 20 at the goal and 30 at the deadline; the Case remains open
At the goal, Urgency resets to 0 and climbs again; at the deadline it locks at 100.
Urgency changes only at the deadline, never at the goal.
At the deadline the Case auto-resolves as 'Resolved-Expired'.

practiceQuiz.hint: Apply the two configured increments; do not assume a universal default action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configured +10 increments yield 20 at the goal and 30 at the deadline, below the 100 cap. Neither event inherently resets urgency or jumps it to 100.

optionExplanations.A: Configured +10 increments yield 20 at the goal and 30 at the deadline, below the 100 cap.
optionExplanations.B: Neither event inherently resets urgency or jumps it to 100.
optionExplanations.C: The goal also has its configured +10 adjustment.
optionExplanations.D: No resolution action is configured in this scenario.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA explains Urgency to a teammate. Which statement is correct about Case Urgency versus Assignment Urgency?

options.text: Case Urgency is the priority of the Case; Assignment Urgency is the priority of one task. An Assignment's initial Urgency equals the Case Urgency value, which defaults to 10.
Case and Assignment Urgency are the same property with two names.
Assignment Urgency defaults to 100 and decreases over time.
Case Urgency is set per user in their Operator record.

practiceQuiz.hint: Two urgencies; initial Assignment Urgency = Case Urgency = default 10.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case priority and task priority are distinct; the task initially uses the Case urgency. They are not merely two names for one property.

optionExplanations.A: Case priority and task priority are distinct; the task initially uses the Case urgency.
optionExplanations.B: They are not merely two names for one property.
optionExplanations.C: An initial value of 100 followed by automatic decay is not the documented default.
optionExplanations.D: The Case Type settings, not an individual operator priority, define the initial Case urgency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Two Assignments are available to a user. Which Pega capability ensures the user is handed the higher-priority one first?

options.text: Get Next Work — it favors the Assignment with the greatest Urgency so high-priority work is completed on time
A Decision Table that ranks Assignments by business data
The work queue's alphabetical sort order
A Data Page that caches Assignments in priority order

practiceQuiz.hint: Highest-Urgency-first Assignment delivery is the purpose of Get Next Work.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Get Next Work favors higher-urgency Assignments the user is eligible to perform. A Decision table can evaluate conditions but is not the named work-selection capability.

optionExplanations.A: Get Next Work favors higher-urgency Assignments the user is eligible to perform.
optionExplanations.B: A Decision table can evaluate conditions but is not the named work-selection capability.
optionExplanations.C: Alphabetical order does not implement urgency-based selection.
optionExplanations.D: Caching data does not by itself deliver the next eligible Assignment.

practiceQuiz.scenario: On which elements of a Case Life Cycle can you configure SLA goals and deadlines?

options.text: Case Type, Stage, Process, and Collect-information/Approval Steps — but NOT the Create Stage
Only the entire Case and individual Steps — Process and Stage SLAs are not supported
Every element including the Create Stage
Only at the Step level; Case/Process/Stage use a separate panel

practiceQuiz.hint: Four levels — and one Stage is excluded.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case, Stage, Process and supported task Steps can have SLAs; the Create Stage is excluded. The documented scopes include Processes and Stages.

optionExplanations.A: Case, Stage, Process and supported task Steps can have SLAs; the Create Stage is excluded.
optionExplanations.B: The documented scopes include Processes and Stages.
optionExplanations.C: The Create Stage is the stated exception.
optionExplanations.D: SLA support is broader than individual Steps.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA tries to set a goal and deadline on the Create Stage of a Case Type and finds it is not allowed. Why?

options.text: The Create Stage collects data before Case processing starts, so SLAs and escalation actions cannot be set on it
SLAs require at least one Step in the Stage, and the Create Stage has none
The Create Stage SLA must instead be configured in Admin Studio
Only Resolution Stages can have SLAs

practiceQuiz.hint: What is special about when the Create Stage runs?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The Create Stage collects information before Case processing starts, so this configuration is unavailable. The exclusion is not explained by an assertion that the Stage has no Steps.

optionExplanations.A: The Create Stage collects information before Case processing starts, so this configuration is unavailable.
optionExplanations.B: The exclusion is not explained by an assertion that the Stage has no Steps.
optionExplanations.C: Changing to Admin Studio does not remove the Create Stage restriction.
optionExplanations.D: Other processing Stages support SLAs; they are not limited to resolution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A child Case's SLA must begin counting from the moment its TOP-LEVEL parent Case was created. Which configuration achieves this?

options.text: Set 'Calculate time from the start of' to Top-level Case
Set 'Calculate time from the start of' to This Case
Use an Existing SLA, which always measures from the top-level Case
Set 'Use SLA' to Never and add a timer Wait instead

practiceQuiz.hint: Calculate time from the start of: This Case / Parent / Top-level.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Top-level Case selects the required start reference for the child’s SLA. This Case would use the child’s own start.

optionExplanations.A: Top-level Case selects the required start reference for the child’s SLA.
optionExplanations.B: This Case would use the child’s own start.
optionExplanations.C: Reusing an SLA does not inherently choose the top-level start reference.
optionExplanations.D: Never removes the SLA rather than selecting its start reference.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A running Case’s urgency is updated from 10 to 25. Does this change alone retroactively rewrite the urgency of its already-open Assignments?

options.text: No; the new Case value is used for new Assignments, not retroactively applied to existing ones
Every open Assignment immediately changes to 25
Open Assignments reset to 10 and recalculate
The change is rejected because Urgency cannot be edited after deployment

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish a Case urgency update from the existing Assignment’s own SLA adjustments.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Updated Case urgency supplies the initial urgency for new Assignments; it does not retroactively change existing ones. Existing Assignments are not automatically rewritten to the new Case value.

optionExplanations.A: Updated Case urgency supplies the initial urgency for new Assignments; it does not retroactively change existing ones.
optionExplanations.B: Existing Assignments are not automatically rewritten to the new Case value.
optionExplanations.C: The change does not inherently reset existing tasks to 10.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario does not establish a prohibition on updating Case urgency.

practiceQuiz.scenario: When an SLA milestone is missed, which set of escalation actions can it run?

options.text: Notify the assignee/manager/participants/creator, reassign the Task, or resolve the Case
Only send an email to the assignee
Only increase Urgency — actions are configured elsewhere
Delete the Case to clear the backlog

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the three types of escalation actions available when an SLA milestone is missed.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Configured escalation can notify recipients, reassign work or resolve the Case. Escalation is not restricted to email for the assignee.

optionExplanations.A: Configured escalation can notify recipients, reassign work or resolve the Case.
optionExplanations.B: Escalation is not restricted to email for the assignee.
optionExplanations.C: Urgency adjustments and additional actions can coexist on the SLA.
optionExplanations.D: Deletion is not the resolution action described by these sources.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Case has an eight-hour deadline with Notify team lead and +10 urgency configured, but no resolution action. What does this deadline configuration imply?

options.text: Notify and adjust urgency when the event is processed; this configuration does not itself close the Case
It auto-closes as 'Resolved-Expired'
It pauses until a supervisor restarts it
It is deleted to prevent backlog

practiceQuiz.hint: Resolution is a separate configured action, not the inevitable meaning of a deadline.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Notification and a configured urgency adjustment do not themselves resolve the Case. No Resolved-Expired outcome is configured here.

optionExplanations.A: Notification and a configured urgency adjustment do not themselves resolve the Case.
optionExplanations.B: No Resolved-Expired outcome is configured here.
optionExplanations.C: Notification does not inherently pause processing for supervisor restart.
optionExplanations.D: The deadline does not inherently delete the Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Inspection shows an existing SLA Rule, but no SLA applied to the Review Step. The Step needs its goal notification. Which configuration is missing?

options.text: Apply the existing SLA to the Review Step
Change the form’s light/dark theme
Rename the reviewer’s Work Queue
Create a report filter for overdue work

practiceQuiz.hint: The scenario gives configuration evidence; a missing email alone would not prove the cause.
practiceQuiz.rationale: An existing SLA must be applied to the relevant work to govern its intervals. Changing the page’s theme does not attach the SLA.

optionExplanations.A: An existing SLA must be applied to the relevant work to govern its intervals.
optionExplanations.B: Changing the page’s theme does not attach the SLA.
optionExplanations.C: Renaming a queue does not apply the SLA to the task.
optionExplanations.D: An overdue-work report does not establish the missing task SLA configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SLA must notify at day 3, reassign at day 7, then resolve still-open work at day 10. Which explicitly configured schedule represents those times?

options.text: Goal day 3: Notify; deadline day 7: Reassign; passed deadline interval 3 days, one event: Resolve
Only a notification at day 7
One goal at day 3 carrying all actions at the same time
Alphabetical Work Queue ordering with no SLA intervals

practiceQuiz.hint: The later action is three days after the deadline; limit it to one passed deadline event.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Goal at day 3, deadline at day 7 and one passed deadline event three days later supply the required schedule. A notification at day 7 does not represent the required reassignment and later resolution.

optionExplanations.A: Goal at day 3, deadline at day 7 and one passed deadline event three days later supply the required schedule.
optionExplanations.B: A notification at day 7 does not represent the required reassignment and later resolution.
optionExplanations.C: One shared milestone cannot express all three stated times.
optionExplanations.D: An alphabetical queue order is not this time-based policy.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is asking an SA where SLAs can be applied in a Pega Case Life Cycle. Which TWO levels support SLA configuration in a Pega application?

options.text: Case Type level — to set an overall deadline for the entire Case
Stage level — to set a deadline for completing all work within a Stage
Field Group level — to enforce data entry time limits on individual fields
Application Settings level — to apply global time constraints across all Case Types

practiceQuiz.hint: Case Type and processing Stage are lifecycle scopes; fields and report settings are not.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case Type scope supplies a deadline for the whole Case. A processing Stage can have its own completion target.

optionExplanations.A: Case Type scope supplies a deadline for the whole Case.
optionExplanations.B: A processing Stage can have its own completion target.
optionExplanations.C: Field Group is not one of the documented lifecycle SLA scopes.
optionExplanations.D: A global application setting is not the Case Type or lifecycle scope described here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is designing a service agreement enforcement strategy. Which TWO statements correctly describe how Pega SLA urgency works?

options.text: Case Urgency expresses the Case’s overall priority, distinct from each Assignment’s priority
Assignment Urgency determines the order in which work appears when using Get Next Work
Urgency values can exceed 100 when multiple SLAs fire escalations simultaneously
SLA urgency resets to zero automatically when the Case moves to a new Stage

practiceQuiz.hint: Remember the two urgency types and the hard cap — urgency has a ceiling value in Pega.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Case urgency expresses Case priority, distinct from individual Assignment priority. Assignment urgency is used in selecting the next eligible work.

optionExplanations.A: Case urgency expresses Case priority, distinct from individual Assignment priority.
optionExplanations.B: Assignment urgency is used in selecting the next eligible work.
optionExplanations.D: A Stage transition does not inherently reset urgency to zero.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which TWO items are the standard completion milestones in the SLA described here?

options.text: Goal — the desired completion time
Deadline — the late threshold
Work Queue — the team queue to route the assignment when the deadline passes
Report Filter — the criteria to identify overdue Cases in a report

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify time milestones; escalation actions still need separate configuration.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Goal is the desired completion milestone, with configurable responses. Deadline is the late threshold, also with configurable responses.

optionExplanations.A: Goal is the desired completion milestone, with configurable responses.
